Deprecation Notice:
The Marketing Version 202510 (Marketing October 2025) will be sunset on October 15, 2026. We recommend that you migrate to the latest versioned APIs to avoid disruptions. For information on all the supported versions, refer to the migrations documentation.
If you haven’t yet migrated and have questions, submit a request on the LinkedIn Developer Support Portal.

The Company Intelligence API delivers company (target account)-level data for all companies engaged through LinkedIn. It provides metrics such as engagement score, paid impressions, paid clicks, leads, paid qualified leads, conversions, paid video views, organic impressions, and organic engagements. Designed to support attribution tools, the API offers accurate company-level data. Use it to gain insights, improve targeting, and measure how companies across your ad accounts interact with your brand on LinkedIn effectively.

The Company Intelligence API delivers company (target account)-level data for all companies engaged through LinkedIn. It provides metrics such as engagement score, paid impressions, paid clicks, leads, paid qualified leads, conversions, paid video views, cost per paid qualified lead (CPQL), organic impressions, and organic engagements, along with firmographic attributes such as company size, industry, and headquarters country/region. Designed to support attribution tools, the API offers accurate company-level data. Use it to gain insights, improve targeting, and measure how companies across your ad accounts interact with your brand on LinkedIn effectively.

The Company Intelligence API delivers company (target account)-level data for all companies engaged through LinkedIn. It provides metrics such as engagement score, paid impressions, paid clicks, leads, paid qualified leads, conversions, paid video views, cost per paid qualified lead (CPQL), organic impressions, and organic engagements, along with firmographic attributes such as company size, industry, and headquarters country/region. You can filter results by campaign, campaign group, objective type, or member seniority. Designed to support attribution tools, the API offers accurate company-level data. Use it to gain insights, improve targeting, and measure how companies across your ad accounts interact with your brand on LinkedIn effectively.

Metrics such as paid qualified leads and conversions are only supported for API versions starting from March 2026 and later.
The paidVideoViews metric is only supported for API versions starting from May 2026 and later.

The companySize, industry, countryCode, and costInLocalCurrencyPerPaidQualifiedLead fields, along with the LAST_365_DAYS lookback window option, are only supported for API versions starting from June 2026 and later.

The paidVideoViews metric is only supported for API versions starting from May 2026 and later.
The companySize, industry, countryCode, and costInLocalCurrencyPerPaidQualifiedLead fields, along with the LAST_365_DAYS lookback window option, are only supported for API versions starting from June 2026 and later.
The campaignGroup, objectiveType, and seniority filter fields are only supported for API versions starting from September 2026 and later.

The developer application must be provisioned with the Company Intelligence API access.
The developer application must be provisioned with the Advertising API access.
The authenticated member must have a valid user role VIEWER or above on the requested ad account for this API.
The authenticated member must have consented to the r_ads_reporting permission of the Advertising API product for your developer app. If the member has already consented through an existing integration (e.g., Ad Analytics API), you can use their existing member access token and do not need to require re-authentication.

This is a private API available only to previously approved developers. We are not currently accepting new applications for the Company Intelligence API. Use the Ad Analytics API for your reporting needs. We will update our recent changes documentation when we are ready to accept new applications.
Use the Company Intelligence API to retrieve company-level paid and organic engagement for a Sponsored Account, using filter criteria.

All results available are returned via the API with no upper limits. You can page through the results using the start and count parameters. You can leverage the href returned under links with rel: next in the response to make your next paginated request in a loop and exit when there are no elements in the response elements:[].
The maximum supported page size (i.e., count parameter) is 1,000. We recommend a smaller page size (count=500 or lower) to prevent server timeout issues.
All impression, engagement, and click metrics must meet specific number thresholds to protect member privacy. If that threshold isn’t met, you’ll see a 0 value for those metrics in the response.
Elements in the response are sorted by paidImpressions in descending order.

Rows.Text: Ad Account URN of the advertiser requesting the account intelligence data. The format is urn:li:sponsoredAccount:1234. The authenticated user must have a valid role on this ad account. For more information, see Find Ad Accounts by Authenticated User API.
Contains filters to apply to the request as described in Company Intelligence Filter Criteria.
Indicates whether to skip fetching companyName in response. Currently returns companyName even if specified true due to an API issue.

The inclusive lookback window in days to filter results. Engagement events are included only if they fall within this lookback range from the day the results are calculated. The lookback window starts approximately 2 days prior to the current date and extends backward 90, 60, 30, or 7 days. The range is rounded to the start of day (00:00 UTC) for the beginning and to the end of day (23:00 UTC) for the end.For example, for a LAST_7_DAYS request sent on 5/21, response data will be from 5/12 00:00 UTC to 5/19 23:00 UTC.If this field is not provided, a default lookback of 90 days is applied.

The collection of ad segment URNs to filter results. You can provide none, one, or multiple ad segments.Example: ["urn:li:adSegment:1234", "urn:li:adSegment:4567"].For more information, see Find Ad Segments by Ad Account API.

You can provide none or one campaign URN to filter results. Multiple campaigns are not supported.Example: urn:li:sponsoredCampaign:1234.For more information, see Search for Campaigns API.Note: Organic metrics will be 0 when the campaign filter is used.

The inclusive lookback window in days to filter results. Engagement events are included only if they fall within this lookback range from the day the results are calculated. The lookback window starts approximately 2 days prior to the current date and extends backward 180, 90, 60, 30, or 7 days. The range is rounded to the start of day (00:00 UTC) for the beginning and to the end of day (23:00 UTC) for the end.For example, for a LAST_7_DAYS request sent on 5/21, response data will be from 5/12 00:00 UTC to 5/19 23:00 UTC.If this field is not provided, a default lookback of 90 days is applied. Note: Pass lookbackWindow:LAST_180_DAYS in the filterCriteria parameter of the accountIntelligence finder query. When no lookback window is specified, the default of 90 days continues to apply.

The collection of ad segment URNs to filter results. You can provide none, one, or multiple ad segments.Example: ["urn:li:adSegment:1234", "urn:li:adSegment:4567"].For more information, see Find Ad Segments by Ad Account API.

You can provide none or one campaign URN to filter results. Multiple campaigns are not supported.Example: urn:li:sponsoredCampaign:1234.For more information, see Search for Campaigns API.Note: Organic metrics will be 0 when the campaign filter is used.
LAST_365_DAYS, LAST_180_DAYS, LAST_90_DAYS, LAST_60_DAYS, LAST_30_DAYS, LAST_7_DAYS

The inclusive lookback window in days to filter results. Engagement events are included only if they fall within this lookback range from the day the results are calculated. The lookback window starts approximately 2 days prior to the current date and extends backward 365, 180, 90, 60, 30, or 7 days. The range is rounded to the start of day (00:00 UTC) for the beginning and to the end of day (23:00 UTC) for the end.For example, for a LAST_7_DAYS request sent on 5/21, response data will be from 5/12 00:00 UTC to 5/19 23:00 UTC.If this field is not provided, a default lookback of 90 days is applied. Note: Pass lookbackWindow:LAST_365_DAYS in the filterCriteria parameter of the accountIntelligence finder query to retrieve a full year of engagement history. When no lookback window is specified, the default of 90 days continues to apply.

The inclusive lookback window in days to filter results. Engagement events are included only if they fall within this lookback range from the day the results are calculated. The lookback window starts approximately 2 days prior to the current date and extends backward 365, 180, 90, 60, 30, or 7 days. The range is rounded to the start of day (00:00 UTC) for the beginning and to the end of day (23:00 UTC) for the end.For example, for a LAST_7_DAYS request sent on 5/21, response data will be from 5/12 00:00 UTC to 5/19 23:00 UTC.If this field is not provided, a default lookback of 90 days is applied. Note: Pass lookbackWindow:LAST_365_DAYS in the filterCriteria parameter of the accountIntelligence finder query to retrieve a full year of engagement history. When no lookback window is specified, the default of 90 days continues to apply.

The collection of ad segment URNs to filter results. You can provide none, one, or multiple ad segments.Example: ["urn:li:adSegment:1234", "urn:li:adSegment:4567"].For more information, see Find Ad Segments by Ad Account API.

You can provide none or one campaign URN to filter results. Multiple campaigns are not supported.Example: urn:li:sponsoredCampaign:1234.For more information, see Search for Campaigns API.Use only one of campaign, campaignGroup, or objectiveType in a request. Organic metrics will be 0 when the campaign filter is used.

You can provide none or one campaign group URN to filter results. Multiple campaign groups are not supported.Example: urn:li:sponsoredCampaignGroup:1234.Use only one of campaign, campaignGroup, or objectiveType in a request. Organic metrics will be 0 when the campaign group filter is used.

You can provide none or one campaign objective type to filter results.Example: BRAND_AWARENESS.Use only one of campaign, campaignGroup, or objectiveType in a request. Organic metrics will be 0 when the objective type filter is used. See list of objectiveType here.

You can provide none or one standardized seniority ID. The Standardized Seniorities API returns id as a number; pass its decimal representation as a string in this field.Example: standardized seniority ID 4 (Senior) is passed as string value "4". In Rest.li finder syntax, scalar string values within a complex query parameter are not enclosed in quotation marks, so the request uses seniority:4.The seniority filter is supported only with LAST_90_DAYS and when campaign, campaignGroup, and objectiveType are not provided. Other combinations return no results. The seniority filter applies to member-attributable paid and organic engagement metrics; paidQualifiedLeads, conversions, and costInLocalCurrencyPerPaidQualifiedLead are not broken down by seniority.
Name of the engaged member’s company (target company). Returns empty string if skipCompanyDecoration is set to true.
URL of the target company's company page on linkedin.com (e.g., http://linkedin.com/company/linkedin).
URL of the target company’s website domain (e.g., https://www.microsoft.com).

The engagement level of the target company is calculated based on the number of paid and organic member engagements, normalized over the selected time range. The possible values are LOW, VERY_LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, VERY_HIGH.
Number of visits to the advertiser's LinkedIn company page, feed impressions, and product page impressions from members in the target company.
Number of interactions with page posts and product pages on the advertiser's LinkedIn company page from members in the target company.
Number of times sponsored ads were shown to members from the target company.
Number of clicks on sponsored ads and ads virally shared from the members of the target company.
Sum of all social actions, clicks to ad landing page, and clicks to LinkedIn company page (chargeable and free).
Number of leads collected from the target company.
Number of qualified leads from Conversions API (CAPI) attributed to the target company. Note: Applicable only from API versions 202603 and later.

The count of conversions based on actions performed by a member after viewing or clicking on an ad. This includes Conversions API (CAPI) and insights tag conversions. Note: Applicable only from API versions 202603 and later.
Number of paid video ad views from target company members within the lookback window. Note: Applicable only from API versions 202605 and later.

The range of the number of staff employed by the target company. Possible values: SIZE_1, SIZE_2_TO_10, SIZE_11_TO_50, SIZE_51_TO_200, SIZE_201_TO_500, SIZE_501_TO_1000, SIZE_1001_TO_5000, SIZE_5001_TO_10000, SIZE_10001_OR_MORE. Note: Applicable only from API versions 202606 and later.
URN of the industry the target company is associated with, based on its primary business activities and products (e.g., urn:li:industry:1). Note: Applicable only from API versions 202606 and later.
ISO country/region code of the target company's headquarters (e.g., US, GB). Note: Applicable only from API versions 202606 and later.

Cost per paid qualified lead (CPQL) attributed to the target company, in the advertiser's local currency. Derived as the ratio of total ad spend over the number of paid qualified leads collected from members of the target company within the lookback window. Note: Applicable only from API versions 202606 and later.
